findings.evidence: Lines 59-62: `generatorCount : ℕ` / `expectedGeneratorCount : ℕ`; line 237-238: `def matchesMetadata ... := P.generatorCount = P.expectedGeneratorCount ∧ ...`; every row in the diff sets both to the same numeral (e.g. `generatorCount := 11` / `expectedGeneratorCount := 11` in BabyMonster).
findings.fix: Delete `expectedGeneratorCount` and let `generatorCount` (documented as the source-stated count) be the single field. Restrict `matchesMetadata`/`matchesMetadata_iff` to `P.transcribed.length = P.expectedRelatorCount`, and update the `example` to match.
findings.issue: The new `generatorCount` field duplicates `expectedGeneratorCount`: both are hand-entered numerals and are equal in every row. `matchesMetadata` (line 238, `P.generatorCount = P.expectedGeneratorCount`) no longer checks anything independent, because the derived `generatorNames.length` it used to compare against is gone.

findings.evidence: Grep for `theorem \w*(_generatorCount|_expectedGeneratorCount) ` in Sporadic/ finds 48 matches in 22 files, two per row (six in Mathieu.lean). Example: `co1Presentation_generatorCount : co1Presentation.generatorCount = 8` and `co1Presentation_expectedGeneratorCount : co1Presentation.expectedGeneratorCount = 8`.
findings.fix: Once `expectedGeneratorCount` is removed, delete every `*_expectedGeneratorCount` theorem and point the docstrings that cite it at `*_generatorCount`.
findings.issue: Every row now has two simp theorems that state the same number: the new `*_generatorCount` and the existing `*_expectedGeneratorCount`. This happens in 22 files: Conway/One, Two, Three; Fischer/TwentyTwo, TwentyThree, TwentyFour; Held; HigmanSims; HaradaNorton; Janko/One, Two, Three, Four; Lyons; Mathieu (3 pairs); Mathieu/TwentyThree; Mathieu/TwentyFour; McLaughlin; Monster; ONan; Rudvalis; Suzuki.

summary: Replacing `generatorNames` with a hand-written `generatorCount` leaves two copies of the same datum next to each other: `generatorCount` and `expectedGeneratorCount`. Every sporadic row now carries a pair of duplicate simp theorems for them, and the generator half of `matchesMetadata` has become a check that two equal numerals match.
